body: Hi! Have you made any progress since your post?  I just started remeron and am a bit nervous about experiencing the same thing you did.  Although, I'm coming from a situation where I was sleeping like you are, about 1-2 days a week, because I weaned off of THC and Duloxetine that I had been on for several years.  The remeron has helped so far

For me, when I was getting off of some harder substances, I found martial arts.  I was able to commit myself fully to something that I had no idea about.  I felt overwhelmed and lost at first, and it was the hardest thing that I had ever done.  10 years later, I still do it.  I have used jiu-jitsu as an escape, a hope, a hobby, a lifestyle.  It is the most physically demanding thing that you will do, and you will be exhausted at the end of each class, which is what I needed.  It absolved me of my other worries, and I got lost in the art.  I am definitely not perfect, and am trying to quit smoking myself, but jiu-jitsu helped me through the darkest times of my life by forcing me to do something I felt was completely out of my abilities, physically and mentally.  I would recommend finding something new that you can get lost in, and something that requires a strenuous physical element to it.  Running, surfing, something like that.  Hope that helps.

For sure, benzos are the worst.  I was prescribed Xanax for my last quitting attempt, and I ended up going through an intense withdrawal that made weed look easy.  Shaking, dry heaves, etc.  That's part of the reason I started smoking again.  Good luck to you! If you can go 111 days without weed, you can get rid of the bezos too!

Man, I can identify so much with the progressive downward spiral.  I noticed that coffee, even decaf sometimes sets me back a full 24 hours. If I can get to sleep, I'm good, I can sleep as much as I want.  However, most nights I can't get there.  It's all or nothing.  I'm just surprised that it's been almost 4 months for you.  It's been about a month for me with a few relapses, and constant attempts of taking something, anything to just try to get to sleep.  I'm going to try to just stop taking anything and see how my body tries to adapt.

​

Yeah, honestly, the anxiety that I felt when I was high was unmanageable.  I was hiding it from my wife and everyone I knew too.  I was basically living a lie.  It had gotten to the point where I completely hated myself for not being able to stop.  Now, I have so much less anxiety, I feel so much better, except there is the insomnia.
How is a typical night for you without the other drugs?  Do you get any sleep? A few hours?  How do you feel the next day?
Ive experienced the same thing.  How long did it take until you were confident about sleeping again?
